claims.text: A post-sintering aging treatment will induce uniformly distributed nanoscale δ-lamellae and/or γ″ precipitates in a W-based refractory high-entropy alloy.
Formation of the δ and γ″ precipitates occurs through a diffusional transformation.
The δ-lamellae and γ″ precipitates are ductile.
Homogeneously distributed δ and γ″ precipitates improve ductility and promote uniform plastic deformation.
The precipitation treatment can preserve high strength while retaining improved tensile ductility.
The treatment will preserve impact-induced energy release.
The as-sintered untreated alloy has a strength of approximately 1 GPa.
The as-sintered untreated alloy has limited ductility and non-optimized plastic deformation.
Aging at approximately 850 °C for 40–50 hours is an effective treatment for producing the desired precipitate structure.
The aging treatment must be conducted under an inert atmosphere.
A homogeneous initial as-sintered microstructure is required for the treatment to be beneficial.
The treatment creates coherent precipitate/matrix interfaces and a homogeneous intragranular precipitate distribution.
Coherent δ/matrix interfaces accommodate large numbers of dislocations during deformation.
The precipitates act as barriers to dislocation pile-ups.
The small size and lattice compatibility of γ″ particles reduce interactions with cutting dislocations and prevent crack initiation at precipitate–matrix interfaces.
Coherent misalignment of sheared δ-lamellae reduces cleavage and avoids microcrack formation at strains above 10%.
The treatment will increase uniform elongation from the untreated baseline to 15–20% or more.
Yield strength will remain around 1 GPa after aging.
Temperatures outside 800–900 °C or excessively long aging will cause overaging, coarsening, or brittle grain-boundary phases that negate ductility and reduce strength.
The untreated alloy's lower ductility is caused by the absence of an optimized nanoscale precipitate structure.

contradictions.description: The target property is described as impact-induced energy release, but the experiment instead measures and requires maintenance of impact energy absorption. Energy release and absorbed impact energy are not interchangeable outcomes and may represent opposing energetic behavior.
